newsitem.title: FRANCE: French food industry cautiously backs gene maize.
newsitem.headline: French food industry cautiously backs gene maize.

text.p: France's food industry on Wednesday cautiously welcomed the approval of Ciba-Geigy's gene-modified maize for sale in the European Union.
But the umbrella group for French food firms said it was important now to ensure the strain could be traced all the way from the farmer to the consumer's plate.
"Our position is that if the product is safe, there is no reason not to use it," said Benoit Mangenot, secretary general of the National Agrofood Industry Association, ANIA.
The European Commission on Wednesday approved the maize which is adapated to resist the corn borer pest and a herbicide and has been grown in the United States this year.
Swiss-based Ciba-Geigy said afterwards it would label the seed bags that contain the special maize.
Mangenot said what was needed was a full system of "traceability" to prove to consumers that the genetically engineered material was sold separately from ordinary maize.
Grain executives said such a system was now widely seen as indispensible to satisfy consumers who pay increasing attention to what they eat following the crisis over mad cow disease.
Some food processing companies have already said they do want the modified maize, they said.
"It is becoming an increasingly important issue," said Roland Wittmann, commodities buyer for Costimex, a maize subsidiary of the big private French grain firm Soufflet.
Distinguishing between the two types of maize will become even more vital when European farmers start copying their U.S. counterparts by producing the maize themselves, he said.
A spokesman for French maize producers earlier welcomed the EU move and said French farmers would start sowing the modified maize as early as next spring if as the seed prices were right.
